Everyday calculations / FIELD GUIDE

How to calculate a discount percentage and final price

Know the final price and how much you save before you buy—or before you announce a sale.

By Manglo Editorial7 November 20266 min read
THE MANGLO PLAYBOOK / ORIGINAL GUIDE

A “30% off” label tells you the percentage reduction, not the exact amount you will pay. The arithmetic is easy once you know the original price. You can use the same formulas for shopping, invoices and planning promotions.

The two basic discount formulas

Discount amount = original price × (discount % ÷ 100)
Final price = original price − discount amount

For an item marked at ₹1,000 with a 20% discount, the reduction is ₹1,000 × 0.20 = ₹200. The customer pays ₹800 before any additional taxes, shipping or fees that may apply.

Quick examples you can check yourself

OriginalDiscountYou saveNew price
₹50010%₹50₹450
₹1,00020%₹200₹800
₹2,00025%₹500₹1,500
₹1,50030%₹450₹1,050
₹80050%₹400₹400

These are arithmetic examples, not current prices at any retailer. The same formulas work with other currencies.

How to find the discount percentage from two prices

Discount % = ((original price − sale price) ÷ original price) × 100

If a ₹1,200 item now costs ₹900, the savings are ₹300. Divide ₹300 by ₹1,200 and multiply by 100: the reduction is 25%. This only works when the stated original price is genuine; the arithmetic cannot verify a store's pricing claims.

Why two discounts don't simply add together

Suppose a ₹1,000 item gets 20% off, then another 10% off the already reduced price. After the first discount it costs ₹800. The second discount is 10% of ₹800, or ₹80, leaving ₹720. Total savings are ₹280, equivalent to 28% of the original—not 30%.

What about tax and delivery?

Check whether a displayed price already includes tax, whether delivery charges apply, and whether a coupon has eligibility conditions. A discount on the product price does not necessarily reduce every part of the final checkout total.

Check the result without mental math

Enter the original price and percentage in the Manglo discount calculator. If you're selling rather than buying, add your product cost to estimate what remains after the reduction. For a fuller estimate including other expenses, use the profit calculator.
